rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test the foundational impact of multimodal fusion. This configuration isolates the effect of combining RNA and image data using standard encoders (pca_n2000 and resnet50) with simple concatenation fusion. It directly addresses whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines, which is critical for guiding subsequent experiments.

The existing evidence shows that the multimodal singleprofile setup with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieves 52.66% accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It directly builds on the previous configuration by modifying a key design choice (fusion) while keeping other components constant, balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~52% accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the effect of image encoder choice. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether the image encoder significantly impacts performance, which is critical for optimizing resource allocation in limited budgets.

Existing evidence shows config_022 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, concat fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.535). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (instead of concat) with the same RNA/image encoders could improve performance. It isolates the effect of fusion method, a key design choice, while keeping other factors constant. This is critical for understanding whether weighted fusion offers better performance than concatenation when using the stronger imagenet_vit_l encoder.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with imagenet_vit_l and concat fusion achieve highest accuracy (0.5353). This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (a key design choice not yet tested), isolating its impact on performance. It balances exploration of profile settings with a logical extension of successful components (resnet50 and concat fusion).

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion (config_018) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests the effect of switching fusion type from concat to weighted while keeping other components constant, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It is a logical extension of the high-performing config_018 and clarifies whether weighted fusion improves performance without altering other critical design choices.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests the RNA encoder (scvi_n200) in the same setup as config_019, isolating the effect of the RNA representation. It addresses uncertainty about whether advanced encoders (like scvi_n200) improve performance compared to pca_n2000, while keeping other parameters consistent for fair comparison.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other parameters the same, isolating the effect of aggregation method. This is a logical extension of the promising direction identified by config_031, balancing exploitation of its success with exploration of a key design choice (aggregation).

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (config_032) achieves high validation accuracy (0.6878). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (vs concat) in the same setup clarifies the impact of fusion strategy. It isolates the effect of fusion method while keeping other key components (aggregation, encoders) consistent, providing critical insight into design choices with limited budget.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced model) while keeping other parameters fixed (scvi_n200 RNA, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) improves performance. This isolates the effect of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and addresses uncertainty about whether more complex image encoders outperform resnet50 in this context.
